blogs.title: The Great Mimic: When Pedunculated Leiomyomas Masquerade as Ovarian Malignancy in Pregnancy
blogs.description: This post dissects the diagnostic dilemma presented by large, cystic, and vascularized abdominal masses in pregnant patients. We explore how pedunculated leiomyomas with degenerative changes can mimic decidualized endometriomas or ovarian tumors on ultrasound and MRI. Key learning points include interpreting the limitations of CA-125 trends during the second trimester, distinguishing uterine vs. adnexal origins when the 'connective stalk' is obscured by gravid anatomy, and knowing when non-contrast MRI is the tie-breaker before committing to surgery.

blogs.title: To Cut or To Wait? Navigating the Threshold for Myomectomy in the Second Trimester
blogs.description: Conservative management is the gold standard for fibroids in pregnancy, but this case highlights the critical exceptions where surgical intervention becomes life-saving. We analyze the specific indications that forced a shift from expectant management to urgent laparotomy: torsion of a pedunculated mass, intractable pain, restrictive lung disease from mass effect, and signs of necrosis/infection. The discussion will weigh the risks of preterm labor against the catastrophic consequences of leaving a twisting, necrotic mass untreated, offering a framework for risk stratification in similar complex cases.

blogs.title: The Partial Solution: Strategic Intraoperative Decision-Making to Preserve Pregnancy
blogs.description: Sometimes the best surgical move is knowing what *not* to remove. This post focuses on the nuanced intraoperative decision to resect only the symptomatic, twisted cranial mass while deliberately leaving the large caudal pelvic myoma in situ. We discuss the rationale behind avoiding extensive dissection near the uterine torus to minimize hemorrhage and uterine irritability, effectively trading a future delivery complication (obstructed labor) for immediate maternal stabilization and fetal preservation. Includes pearls on intraoperative fetal monitoring and progesterone prophylaxis.

blogs.title: Mass Effect Mechanics: Recognizing Non-Obstetric Causes of Dyspnea and Abdominal Pain in Late Second Trimester
blogs.description: Dyspnea and abdominal pain are common complaints in pregnancy, often attributed to normal physiological changes or obstetric emergencies like abruption or preterm labor. This case serves as a reminder to evaluate for mechanical compression from extra-uterine or large uterine pathology. We review how massive leiomyomas can elevate the diaphragm causing restrictive lung disease and compress adjacent organs, mimicking acute abdomen scenarios. The post emphasizes the importance of thorough bimanual exams and targeted imaging when vital signs are stable but symptom severity is disproportionate to gestational age.

blogs.title: Planning the Exit Strategy: How Antepartum Myomectomy Dictates Mode of Delivery
blogs.description: Surgical management of fibroids during pregnancy doesn't end at closure; it fundamentally alters the birth plan. Using this case as a blueprint, we discuss how the presence of a remaining large posterior myoma necessitates an elective Cesarean section to prevent obstructed labor and uterine rupture during expulsion. We examine the timing of delivery (37 weeks), the choice of incision (re-using the laparotomy scar), and counseling points regarding future fertility and the potential need for delayed myomectomy post-partum versus spontaneous regression.
